This counter counts hold-vector-issue cycles for [matmul_path_reserved](http://go/gfc-isa#matmul-path-reserved). (Reservations only count if the associated instruction's predication evaluates to true.)

This counter counts hold-vector-issue cycles for [matmul_accumulation_pipe_reserved](http://go/gfc-isa#matmul-accumulation-pipe-reserved). (Reservations only count if the associated instruction's predication evaluates to true.)
This counter increments for each Q128 imem write.

This counter increments when a DMA write to Imem must wait more that 16 cycles due to conflicting accesses by instructions that use Imem.  Once the initial 16 cycles of waiting have passed, the counter increments for each additional contiguous cycle of delay. (This counter is an Alarm Counter; it is expected to typically remain zero.)

limitations: Instruction timestamps and widths are reconstructed by XProf between hardware trace points.
Occurrence alignment can shift after dropped events; matched fraction does not prove completeness.
Per-source and per-unit spans overlap; coverage is not additive hardware stall time.
Same-binary repeatability uses call 0 timestamps and is a replay baseline, not a prediction.
Count floor assumes 2.2 GHz, BF16 8-cycle issue and incomplete observed dynamic work.
Full physical MRB, DMA dependencies, actual clock and matching backend schedule remain required.
